test_title: RRB Technician Grade III Official Paper (Held On: 26 Dec, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Tap S alone fills a cistern in 2 hours; while tap T alone fills the same cistern in 3 hours. A new tap U is attached to the bottom of the cistern which can empty the completely filled cistern in 6 hours. Sunny started all three taps together at 9 a.m. When will the tank be full?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Capacity (LCM of 2, 3, 6) = 6 units.

Net efficiency = S + T − U = (6/2) + (6/3) − (6/6) = 3 + 2 − 1 = 4 units/hour.

Time taken = Total Capacity ÷ Net efficiency = 6/4 = 1.5 hours.

Time = 9:00 a.m. + 1 hour 30 minutes = 10:30 a.m.

**∴ The correct answer is 10:30 a.m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Tap **S** fills in 2 hours, Tap **T** fills in 3 hours, Tap **U** (outlet) empties in 6 hours.

**Formula Used:** Total Work = Time × Efficiency; Net Efficiency = Σ Efficiency (Filling − Emptying).

 
 **Tap** **Time (hrs)** **Total Work (LCM)** **Efficiency** 
 S (Fill) 2 6 units +3 
 T (Fill) 3 +2 
 U (Empty) 6 −1 

⇒ Total efficiency when all taps are open = 3 + 2 − 1 = 4 units/hour.

⇒ Total time required = 6 ÷ 4 = 1.5 hours.

⇒ 1.5 hours = 1 hour 30 minutes.

⇒ Start time = 9:00 a.m. Final time = 9:00 a.m. + 1:30 = 10:30 a.m.

**∴ The correct answer is 10:30 a.m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes & Cisterns Efficiency

Filling pipes have positive efficiency, while emptying/outlet pipes have negative efficiency. Net rate = Rateᵢₙ − Rateₒᵤₜ.

Combined Time Formula

For two filling pipes A and B and one outlet C, the time taken (T) is given by 1/T = 1/A + 1/B − 1/C.

Work & Wages

Wages are always distributed in the ratio of the efficiency or the actual work done by each pipe/tap.</p
